note: Wave-2 graded items for class 11 Sociology pools (kesy101-205). One-term factual keys; machine-graded.

questions.q: Mass joblessness, unlike one person's joblessness, is a fact about what?
Which discipline links personal biography to social structure?
The sociological imagination connects biography to history or to biology?

concepts.title: The Emergence of Sociology in Europe

questions.q: In which century was sociology born in Europe?
Which revolution shaped politics at sociology's birth: the French or the Industrial?
Which transformation of work and city life formed sociology's economic backdrop?
Which colonial exercise counted castes ten-yearly from 1881?
After independence, Indian sociology turned to nation-building, development and what third purpose?
Indian sociology grew from the colonial archive and from whose own traditions of inquiry?
Which discipline abstracts the market from social life?
Which discipline studies the state?
Which discipline studies the past in sequence?

concepts.title: Social Groups: Aggregate, Category and Quasi-Group

questions.q: People physically together, like a bus queue, form an aggregate or a group?
People alike in one trait, like all tall persons, form a what?
A set with common interests but no organisation yet is called a what group?
Caste is an ascribed or an achieved status?
The behaviour expected of whoever holds a status is called a what?
A status earned through effort is called what?
Norms backed by sanctions exert what?
The largest web of relationships marked by self-sufficiency is called a what?
Which smaller grouping is held together by locality and belonging?
Is culture learned or inherited biologically?
Tools, dress and buildings form which culture: material or non-material?
The nature versus nurture debate weighs biological instinct against what?
Which institution is organised around kinship and care?
Which institution organises power?
Institutions look natural but are what: human constructions or divine gifts?
Marriage within one's own group is called what?
The marriage of one man to several wives is called what?
Descent traced through the father's line is called what?
Power accepted as legitimate is called what?
Name Weber's authority type resting on laws and offices: legal-rational, traditional or charismatic?
Modern states monopolise legitimate what within a territory?
Which institution organises the production and distribution of livelihood?
Which institution deals with the sacred?
Which institution transmits knowledge and values?
Ideas and customs form which culture: material or non-material?
Culture is learned and what else: shared or secret?
Do material and non-material culture change together or separately?
Which dimension of culture covers what people know: cognitive or normative?
Which dimension covers what people ought to do?
A flag or a gesture carries meanings of which dimension: symbolic or cognitive?
The lifelong process turning a newborn into a social person is called what?
Socialisation in the family forms which personality: basic or secondary?
School, peers and media resocialise the individual into new what?
Is the self formed socially or in isolation?
Gender, caste and nationality are examples of what?
Individuality matures only inside a web of what?
Sociology earns the name of science mainly through what: method or laboratories?
Objectivity for the sociologist means disciplined self-awareness about one's own what?
Whose reactions make controlled experiment hard: humans' or chemicals'?
Interviews and observation collect which data: primary or secondary?
Censuses and official reports are which data?
Newspapers used as research material are what kind of source?

concepts.title: The Survey, Sampling and the Questionnaire

questions.q: Selecting a smaller set chosen to represent the whole is called what?
Which instrument collects survey answers in writing?
A survey asks standardised questions of many respondents to map what across a population?
Living among the people studied is called what kind of observation?
Qualitative interviews let respondents speak in their own what?
Fieldwork trades scale for what: depth or speed?
The recurring organised patterns arranging society's members are called social what?
Families, castes, classes and offices are parts of the social what?
Social structure is invisible as a thing yet visible in its what?

Caste boundaries are kept by which marriage rule?
Class ranking rests mainly on what position: economic or ritual?
Joining efforts toward shared goals is called what?
The rule-bound race for scarce goods is called what?
The collision where parties seek to nullify each other is called what?
Transformation over time of institutions and relationships is called social what?
Do established interests welcome or resist rearrangement?
Does change travel evenly or unevenly across social domains?
The patterned predictability of social life is called social what?
Is social order a natural state or an accomplishment?
Social order can break down in revolution, war or what?
Which society runs on dense face-to-face ties: rural or urban?
What anchors village life economically: agriculture or industry?
In cities, what fills the gaps that intimacy fills in villages?

concepts.title: Ecology of the City and Rural Change

questions.q: Sorting land into commercial, industrial and residential use is called what?
Are villages frozen in time or works in progress?
New crops, roads and schooling dissolve which old image of the village?
Which study examines how living beings relate to their habitat?
Societies draw materials from nature and return what to it?
Does the society-environment relationship run one way or both ways?
Which ecological trouble involves rising average temperatures: climate change or species loss?
Who usually suffers environmental damage first and worst: the poor or the rich?
Ecological troubles flow from how societies produce, consume and what?
Which Indian movement hugged trees to stop contractors felling them: Chipko or Narmada?
Struggles against large dams centre on which river valley: the Narmada or the Ganga?

Which event upheaved politics and posed problems old frameworks could not answer?

Which religious ethic did Weber credit with helping birth capitalism: the Protestant ethic or the Buddhist?

For Mukerji, tradition was dead custom or a dynamic inheritance?

Lower groups adopting the customs of higher groups is called what?
Whose intensive village fieldwork produced the concept of sanskritisation?
